conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you today. I understand you’ve been having abdominal pain, nausea, and diarrhea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. It started a few days ago—sharp pain in the middle of my belly, going to my back. Feels just like my old pancreatitis flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And the nausea—any vomiting?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No vomiting, but the nausea is constant. And the diarrhea—it looks oily, like it floats.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That can happen with pancreatitis when the pancreas isn’t making enough enzymes. We’ve checked your blood, and your lipase is mildly elevated at 86, which supports that idea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that high? Last time it was over 100.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s on the lower end, but still above normal. Given your history, we’re treating this as a mild flare of your chronic pancreatitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ve been taking my usual pain meds, but they’re not helping much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you IV fluids and start you on IV pain medication to help. You’ll also need to rest your bowel for now—no food at first, then we’ll slowly reintroduce it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. I haven’t had much appetite anyway.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. You’ve been doing well. Your vitals are stable, and your pain seems a bit better. We’re going to try a soft diet—start with clear liquids and see how you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds good. Can I have some broth?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with broth and jello. If you keep that down, we’ll advance your diet tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs this morning look stable. Your lipase is trending down, and liver tests are normal. You made it through the night without nausea or pain worsening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel much better. I even had a soft roll this morning with no problem.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’ll keep you on a soft diet for now. Since you’re improving, we’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Should I take anything for nausea or pain at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re prescribing prochlorperazine for nausea if it comes back, and oxycodone 5 mg for pain, just as needed. But use them sparingly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my regular meds—should I keep taking those?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, continue all your home medications—venlafaxine, imipramine, trazodone, prazosin, clonazepam, and ranitidine. They’re important for your mood and GI health.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the diarrhea? Should I be worried?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s likely due to poor fat digestion from your pancreas. If it continues, your GI doctor might adjust your enzyme supplements. For now, watch your diet—low fat, small meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. When should I follow up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Please see your GI doctor soon. And if you develop fever, worsening pain, vomiting, or can’t keep food down, come back right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve reviewed everything, and you’re ready to go home. Your abdomen is soft, you’re walking, and you’ve tolerated food well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m glad it wasn’t worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and don’t hesitate to reach out if symptoms return.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.
